acceptanceCriteria: A call that outlives its caller still commits exactly once.
Refusals are returned verbatim, not as a generic timeout.
--wait returns within its bound plus a small margin.
A holder with a live attempt gets that attempt back, not a second claim.
Tests cover a caller killed mid-claim.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1005 (author ls-russell-lewis, opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Under load claim/pool acquire can outlive the host's per-tool-call limit (~120 s); the caller cannot tell whether the mutation committed. Proposal: --detach starts the mutation in its own process session under the request id and returns a handle; --attach/--wait N returns CLAIMED, PENDING or the verbatim refusal; same holder+request id never starts a second mutation. See beamfall/corvint#1005 for the full problem, current workaround and proposal.
title: corvint-tasks: claim / pool acquire --detach and --attach so a slow mutation survives the caller's tool-call timeout (issue #1005)
